2A. PROFIT POOL MAP
──────────────────────────────────────────

2A.1 Value chain
[AI Infrastructure & Hardware]: <20% gross margin | Concentrated (Nvidia, Huawei) | Expanding | Asset-heavy
[Cloud IaaS & PaaS]: 25–35% gross margin | Concentrated (Alibaba, Tencent, Huawei) | Expanding | Asset-heavy

[AI Applications & Enterprise SaaS]: 70–80% gross margin | Fragmented | Expanding | Asset-light

2A.2 Company position
Alibaba sits at the nexus of the Cloud IaaS and E-commerce Platform layers. It is aggressively moving "up" into high-margin AI Applications (via Qwen models) and "down" into asset-heavy Quick Commerce. Rationale: defending core e-commerce market share via customer lock-in (instant delivery) and capturing the next high-margin layer (enterprise AI workloads) to offset e-commerce margin compression.

2A.3 Material one-time events
- Divestment of physical retail (Sun Art Retail, InTime): Alibaba completed the sale of these non-core physical assets in FY2026 to streamline the balance sheet and focus on digital core [3].
- Massive Capex Acceleration: Capex spiked to ¥126.9B in FY2026 (up ~46% YoY), driven by AI infrastructure procurement (GPUs, data centers). Management confirmed a 3-year, RMB 380B capex plan [1]. This strategic acceleration caused FY2026 FCF to turn negative (-¥50.7B) despite positive operating cash flow.

2A.4 Revenue definition check
Official 10-K / Annual Report FY2026 GAAP Total Revenue: ¥1,023.7B.
Management frequently cites a pro-forma metric "excluding Sun Art and InTime" (divested businesses) which showed ~11–15% YoY growth in recent quarters [2], versus the reported GAAP growth of ~2.7% (FY26) or 9% (Q1 FY27).
FLAG: REVENUE DISCREPANCY. The pro-forma growth rate exceeds the reported GAAP growth rate by >5 percentage points. All YoY growth rate calculations in this report use the GAAP Total Revenue (consolidated) as reported in the Annual Report FY2026 [3].

deep_research_sections.2b:
2B. COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE
──────────────────────────────────────────

2B.1 Market structure classification
Regulated oligopoly transitioning to a winner-take-most dynamic in AI cloud infrastructure, and a fragmented/subsidy-driven oligopoly in e-commerce and quick commerce.

2B.2 Market share map
- E-commerce (GMV): Alibaba ~32% (declining from 50%+ peak); PDD ~23% (rapidly expanding); JD.com ~20% (stable). Price-driven gains by PDD are structurally pressuring Alibaba's take-rate. (Source: JPMorgan / Momentum Works, 2025–2026) [11].
- Cloud IaaS: Alibaba ~22% (Market leader); Huawei ~19%; Tencent ~16%. (Source: IDC / CAICT 2024 Cloud Blue Book) [35][41].
- Quick Commerce (Food Delivery/Instant Retail): Meituan ~60%; Ele.me (Alibaba) ~10%; JD ~10%. (Source: JPMorgan / TechBuzzChina, Nov 2025) [78][97].

2B.3 Basis of competition
1. Price / Subsidy (E-commerce & Quick Commerce): Alibaba spent ~¥83.7B in marketing subsidies in late 2025 to defend share against PDD and Meituan [26][78]. This is a price-driven, margin-eroding dynamic.
2. AI Performance & Ecosystem (Cloud): Customers buy on GPU availability, proprietary model performance (Qwen), and integration costs.
3. Logistics Speed (Quick Commerce): 30-minute delivery capability is the new switching cost.

2B.4 Competitive response profile
When Alibaba gains share in quick commerce via subsidies, competitors (Meituan) respond with matching price cuts and heavy AI/logistics investment, leading to industry-wide margin compression rather than volume expansion [76][94]. In cloud, competitors are racing to secure limited GPU supply.

2B.5 New entrant threat
- AI-native attacker: High (e.g., Zhipu AI, Moonshot). Timeline: 2–3 years. Barrier: Massive compute capex required.
- Vertically integrated customer: Medium (Large enterprises building private clouds).
- Low-cost geographic entrant: Low.

deep_research_sections.2c:
2C. MOAT ANALYSIS
──────────────────────────────────────────

2C.1 PRIMARY moat source
Switching costs (E-commerce merchant ecosystem lock-in + Cloud IaaS technical integration).

2C.2 Moat verdict
- Evidence: 900M+ annual active consumers and a massive, deeply integrated merchant base that relies on Taobao/Tmall for distribution and Alibaba Cloud for infrastructure [12][36].
- Direction (3-yr):
  Gross margin [−] (heavy quick commerce subsidies absorbing profits)
  Retention [=]
  Pricing power [−] (PDD price wars)
  Market share [+ / −] (Cloud share +, E-commerce share −)
  ROIC vs WACC spread [−] (due to ¥126.9B capex spike)
  Verdict: **Moat Erosion Risk** flagged. While the cloud moat is widening, the core e-commerce moat is narrowing under sustained subsidy warfare and PDD disruption.
- Stress test: If Alibaba's cloud margin expansion (from AI workloads) fails to materially offset the structural margin compression in core e-commerce caused by Pinduoduo and the quick commerce subsidy burn rate.

deep_research_sections.2d:
2D. INDUSTRY CYCLE POSITIONING
──────────────────────────────────────────

2D.1 Industry lifecycle stage
- E-commerce: Late maturity / Shakeout (consolidating to 3–4 major players).
- Cloud / AI: Early growth (China cloud market expected to triple by 2027, growing at ~30%+ CAGR) [100].

2D.2 Cyclical vs structural demand
- ~70% of current revenue is structurally growing (AI cloud, international commerce) but heavily masked by the cyclical weakness in Chinese consumer spending and the deliberate margin sacrifice in quick commerce.
- Mid-cycle EBITDA is significantly higher than FY2026 reported EBITA (which was depressed by an ~84% plunge in core profitability in Q4 FY2026 due to subsidy spikes and capex absorption) [59][60].

2D.3 Capacity and supply dynamics
Massive AI capacity expansion underway. Alibaba guided a 3-year RMB 380B capex budget, with Q1 FY27 alone seeing RMB 67.7B in capex [68]. GPU capacity is currently supply-constrained; pricing power emerges only when proprietary AI chips (T-Head) or domestic alternatives (Huawei Ascend) are fully deployed to offset US export controls.

2D.4 Inventory cycle
Alibaba operates a predominantly asset-light e-commerce model (merchant-held inventory), though its Cainiao logistics network manages significant transiting inventory. Channel inventory levels for consumer electronics and durables in China remain elevated, reflecting sluggish consumer demand [2].

deep_research_sections.2e:
2E. DISRUPTION & STRUCTURAL CHANGE VECTORS
──────────────────────────────────────────

2E.1 Technology disruption vectors
- Generative AI (Qwen models): Enhances core business. Timeline: 2–5 years. Probability: High. Company response: Leading (investing RMB 380B over 3 years, AI revenue run-rate approaching $10B) [68].
- Domestic Semiconductor Self-Sufficiency: Enhances long-term supply chain resilience. Timeline: >5 years.

2E.2 Regulatory and policy change vectors
- Tailwinds: Chinese government mandates for domestic cloud adoption and AI industrialization [100].
- Headwinds: US export controls on advanced AI chips (H100/B200) restricting Alibaba's ability to train top-tier models without relying on lower-yield domestic chips [60].

2E.3 Business model disruption
- Quick Commerce (30-min delivery) is disrupting traditional 2–3 day e-commerce. Penetration is rapidly increasing across non-food categories. Alibaba is matching Meituan's subsidies but expects FY2029 profitability [1][29].

2E.4 3-year industry structure question
- Competitors: Fewer credible e-commerce players (consolidation).
- Margins: Higher in Cloud (AI monetization), lower in E-commerce (permanent subsidy cost).
- Evidence: Alibaba's cloud external revenue grew 45% in Q1 FY27, while core e-commerce margins plunged. The data point that changes this view: A sudden cessation of the quick commerce subsidy war, leading to immediate margin normalization.

2F.3 CORE FRANCHISE KPIs:

2F.4 OPERATING LEVERAGE:
- Operating margin trajectory: Operating margin compressed significantly in recent quarters (core profit plunged 84% YoY in Q4 FY2026) due to heavy AI capex and quick commerce subsidies [59].

We agree with Goldman's cloud acceleration thesis and its capex-ROIC visibility argument (payback within 3 years, improving toward 2–2.5 years), but our PT of HK$135.69 is materially more conservative than Goldman's street TP of HK$186.00, reflecting Pentagon-listing tail risk and the front-loaded capex drag that their base case discounts more aggressively than we do.\n2. Valuation: our 12-month PT of HK$135.69 is anchored to a blended IV of HK$162.08, with the discount reflecting execution risk; the valuation method is a blended DCF/SOTP using a 12.6% WACC, a base-case DCF IV of HK$163.46 (bear HK$118.33, bull HK$212.97), and a scenario EV of HK$160.60 (+46.9% to spot), cross-checked against a 24.1x fwd P/E and 15.3x EV/EBITDA peer comp — the gap to intrinsic value is the source of the asymmetric return. The macro regime is risk-on / low-vol / near-zero recession probability, supporting multiple expansion for AI-levered names with record ETF inflows; this regime caps conviction at current position sizing rather than full deployment.\n3. The primary risk is the Pentagon's reported move (Bloomberg, ~19 Sep 2026) to add Alibaba to its Chinese military-company list, which could trigger forced selling by US-domiciled funds and widen the ADR/HK discount — this is a genuine binary overhang that Goldman's HK$186.00 TP does not explicitly price.
